content:
alex_cs: Tia from Nova Labs is seeing a tight burst of 429s right after SDK init. They enabled our 'rapid-retry' helper and now the sdkgateway pool looks exhausted. Can eng take a quick look?

 tia_novalabs: Yep, we flip the retry on to handle transient 504s, but within ~30s of startup we see auth success then a flood of retries. App-level logs attached (snip):

 tia_novalabs: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z INFO Auth handshake succeeded for key: pk_***
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z WARN Request failed 429: rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z INFO Retrying (attempt 1) /v1/generate
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z INFO Retrying (attempt 2) /v1/generate
... many concurrent retries ...
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR conn_pool: no healthy upstreams
```

 mika_engineer: Thanks. Two quick hypothesis: (1) client retries without jitter causing synchronized fanout; (2) token refresh / auth TTL causing many clients to re-auth at same second.

 sam_support: Temporary mitigation we often push to customers: turn off aggressive immediate retries and add exponential backoff + jitter. Also set maxAttempts to 3.

 jen_prod: We rolled a change to the sdkgateway default retry policy yesterday (deploybot posted), which switched default maxAttempts from 2->5 for certain error classes. Might be contributing.

 deploybot: Deployment 2026-03-14T22:40:02 UTC: sdkgateway v3.9.1 applied. Change-log: adjusted client-side retry defaults for better throughput under transient 504.

 rory_sre: If you can, capture the Retry-After header on the 429s. If upstream returns Retry-After and clients ignore it, they'll keep hammering. Also check if our auth microservice returned a 200 but with a slightly different scope, triggering later auth-refresh attempts across hosts.

 tia_novalabs: We see Retry-After: 10 sometimes, but most 429s lack it. Token scope looks correct, keys are a standard integration key.

 mika_engineer: Two pragmatic fixes we can A/B: (A) patch sdkgateway to enforce per-client circuit-breaker on 429 bursts (short pause for same client IP/key), (B) update SDK default to include randomized jitter and cap concurrency to gateway. Which do you want faster?

 tia_novalabs: Prefer quick SDK change on our side if it's faster for you to validate. We control the client binary.

 sam_support: Suggested SDK config snippet we recommend to customers:

 sam_support: ```json
{
  "retry": {
    "enabled": true,
    "maxAttempts": 3,
    "initialBackoffMs": 200,
    "maxBackoffMs": 2000,
    "jitter": true
  },
  "concurrency": {
    "maxRequestsPerHost": 10,
    "connectionPoolSize": 8
  }
}
```

 mika_engineer: Also add a client-side token cache TTL (e.g. 5m) with randomized refresh window to avoid many clients re-requesting tokens at identical times.

 jen_prod: On the server side we'll add a short-term mitigation: if a single API key triggers > X 429s in Y seconds, mark a soft hold and return Retry-After consistently. That buys time for client changes. I'll open a rollout ticket.

 alex_cs: Action items: (1) Tia will update their SDK to the snippet and re-test (ETA: 2 hrs). (2) Jen will create a server-side soft-hold threshold and ensure sdkgateway returns Retry-After (ETA: EOD). (3) Mika to validate token refresh jitter behavior in SDK docs (ETA: PR in next day).

 tia_novalabs: Will try SDK patch now and report back. Thanks. :pray:

 rory_sre: Quick note — if customers are on older SDKs we should surface the recommendation in the onboarding checklist so they don't hit this in future.

 sam_support: I'll add a KB article with the config snippet and common triage steps (collect Retry-After, conn_pool errors, token TTL).

 tia_novalabs: Update: after disabling the old rapid-retry and applying the config above, initial spike dropped to single-digit 429s and then stabilized. Looks much better. :thumbsup:

 alex_cs: Awesome — marking this resolved for now. Reopen if you see a recurrence.

 ops_bot: Incident detection: sdkgateway 429 rate for key pk_*** returned to baseline at 2026-03-15T16:10:01Z.
